images.title: Common multiples 30 apart
images.purpose: Show that the numbers both jumpers land on, 30, 60 and 90, are each 30 more than the one before: the multiples of the first common multiple.
images.composition: One number line from 0 to 90 with a row of teal dots for jumps of 6 above it, a row of amber dots for jumps of 15 below it, three purple boxes on 30, 60 and 90 and three arrows saying 30 more.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. A horizontal number line, dark #2B2B2B, 5 px thick, at y 520 from x 100 to x 1356 with an arrowhead at the right end, with exactly 4 tall ticks (30 px) at the numbers 0, 30, 60 and 90: x 128, 528, 928 and 1328 (the scale is 1200 px for 90, so 13.3 px for each whole number). Under the ticks, centred at y 640, the numbers 0, 30, 60 and 90 (36 px, bold, dark #1F2937). ABOVE the line, on a row at y 470: exactly 15 teal #0072B2 dots (16 px across), one at each multiple of 6 from 6 to 90 (6, 12, 18, ..., 90). BELOW the line, on a row at y 570: exactly 6 amber #E69F00 dots (18 px across), one at each multiple of 15 from 15 to 90 (15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90). Exactly 3 thin dashed grey #6B7280 vertical lines from y 440 to y 600 at x 528, 928 and 1328, joining the teal dot and the amber dot at 30, 60 and 90. Exactly 3 reddish purple #CC79A7 rectangles, 6 px outline, no fill, 90 by 60 px, around the numbers 30, 60 and 90 at y 640. Exactly 3 reddish purple curved arrows above the teal row, 5 px thick with arrowheads, each 60 px high: from 0 to 30, from 30 to 60 and from 60 to 90, with the text 30 more (36 px, dark, bold) centred above each at x 328, 728 and 1128 and y 340. Top left, a legend: a teal dot with the text jumps of 6 at x 150 and y 110, and an amber dot with the text jumps of 15 at x 150 and y 180 (36 px, dark). At the bottom, centred at x 728 and y 745, the text 30, 60, 90 are the multiples of 30 in bold dark #1F2937 (46 px). No other text. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The common multiples of two numbers are the multiples of their first common multiple.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 90 with jumps of 6 and jumps of 15 meeting at 30, 60 and 90, each 30 more than the one before.
images.context: Concept image for The Pattern in Common Multiples. It follows the idea of the common multiples of 3 and 6 and 3 and 4 in your maths book and uses this concept's own example, jumps of 6 and 15.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say the gap between the purple boxes before saying the rule. The slip to watch is thinking the list of common multiples stops at 90.

image_decisions.why: The gaps of 30 between the three meeting places make the pattern of common multiples visible.
